about: Round PROG1 (Karl, 2 Nov 2026: "add ways to make progression more tangible and 'fun' JRPG style"; the design is the Project doc claude/HANDOVER_PROGRESSION_2026-11-02.md). The Adventure's progression numbers, one file so Karl tunes them without code. EVERY value is a placeholder (Claude's estimate, 3 Nov 2026) until prog-tune measures them. results: how the screen after a duel plays out, in seconds. card_quality (Round PROG1b; it was meter, the deck-power meter, and a file with meter still reads): the Card quality line - change_seconds the +0.1 shows, decimals, and explain, the one line saying what it is (Karl to edit). rpg/progress.py checks this file when it is read and names any key it can't use. Round PROG2: rewards - how many cards each reward card is a choice of (choices_per_card); boss - whether a boss gives the 'Guards:' card he holds on top of his reward cards; chests - each treasure chest's contents by its id (the map's chest marker names it): gold (a number), card ("band": a card from the region's tier band in your deck's colours), pack (a set code with a pack pool, opened at once), gear (gold until gear exists, Round PROG4: the number is the gold), daily (true: it fills again at refill_hour each in-game morning; otherwise it opens once). Round PROG3: xp - XP a duel gives by kind of foe when won (regular, dungeon, rare, boss), a quest handed in (quest), a lost or conceded duel (loss) and a draw (draw). levels - the curve: level 2 at 'first' XP, each next level needs 'step' more than the last; 'cap' the highest level; every level above 1 adds life_per_level to the duel's starting life (base_life at level 1); every perk_every-th level deals a choice of perk_choices perks. perks - each perk's name, text (what the choice says), stackable (offered again once taken), available (false: never offered - the game can't do it yet; why_not says why) and effect: reward_choices (+N cards per reward pick), gold_bonus (a share added to a win's gold), loss_cut (Round GOLD1: how much smaller a loss is - 0.25 takes a quarter less of numbers.json's share for that kind of fight; it was loss_share, a share instead of numbers.json's), life / hand (added to the duel's start), battlefield (cards on your battlefield at the start; token:SCRIPT is one of Forge's token scripts). rpg/levels.py reads and checks these.

card_quality.explain: The average tier of your cards: how often tournament players use them. Not how strong your deck is - the curve and counts matter as much.
